acceptance_criteria.criterion: Sortable column headers display a pointer cursor on hover
Hovered sortable headers lighten from muted header color to full text color
Active sort column displays ↑ (ascending) or ↓ (descending) immediately after the column label text
Arrow is absent on non-active sortable columns and on the non-sortable Actions column
Rules apply correctly in both light and dark themes
No existing table styles are altered

summary: All 4 CSS rules for sortable table headers are present in mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css (lines 511–524) within a dedicated '/* Sortable column headers */' section. Rules: th.sortable { cursor: pointer; user-select: none }, th.sortable:hover { color: var(--color-text) }, th.sort-asc::after { content: ' ↑' }, th.sort-desc::after { content: ' ↓' }. All existing table styles are unmodified. Implementation was already complete from prior work.

comments.note: Sortable CSS rules landed at line 511 rather than immediately after the '/* Tables */' block (line 164). Functionally correct but slightly out of placement spec in WP-002. No behavioral impact.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified by static inspection of mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css and mcp-server/gui/public/app.js.
AC1 (pointer cursor): th.sortable { cursor: pointer; user-select: none } present at line 513.
AC2 (hover lightens): th default color is var(--color-text-muted) (line 184); th.sortable:hover overrides to var(--color-text) (line 517–519) — correct lightening in both directions.

AC3 (active arrow): th.sort-asc::after { content: ' ↑' } and th.sort-desc::after { content: ' ↓' } at lines 520–524. JS thSort() applies class 'sortable sort-asc' or 'sortable sort-desc' exclusively to the active column.
AC4 (arrow absent elsewhere): non-active columns receive only 'sortable' class; Actions <th> is a plain element with no data-sort and no class — click handler guards with closest('th[data-sort]').

AC5 (both themes): --color-text and --color-text-muted defined in light :root (lines 19–20) and dark @media block (lines 42–43). CSS variables propagate correctly through both themes without any theme-specific overrides needed.
AC6 (no existing table styles altered): existing th {} block at line 178 is unchanged. All new rules are confined to the '/* Sortable column headers */' section (lines 511–524).

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. The four CSS rules are minimal, correctly scoped, and use existing design tokens (--color-text, --color-text-muted) which are already defined for both light and dark themes, requiring no additional theme overrides.

summary: CSS: 4 rules in a well-commented '/* Sortable column headers */' section (styles.css lines 511–524). Minimal and correctly scoped — th.sortable applies cursor+user-select, th.sortable:hover uses the existing --color-text token, th.sort-asc::after and th.sort-desc::after use CSS pseudo-elements for arrows. All existing table styles at lines 164–210 are untouched.

JS: thSort() helper correctly assigns class='sortable' always and appends 'sort-asc' or 'sort-desc' only on the active column — ensuring arrows are absent elsewhere. aria-sort attribute on each th gives correct accessibility semantics. The Actions <th> is a plain element with no data-sort, excluded from the click handler's closest('th[data-sort]') guard.

sortProjects() is well-structured — list.slice() prevents mutation, dates parsed with Date.getTime() for correct chronological ordering, strings sorted with localeCompare. The 'done' column computes a completion ratio with a safe 0 fallback for projects with no WPs.
Click handler uses event delegation on thead, toggles direction on same-column re-click, defaults timestamps to desc and other columns to asc, and persists state to localStorage on every interaction.
All 6 acceptance criteria are met. Code is consistent with the existing ES5-compatible vanilla JS style used throughout app.js.

comments.note: styles.css: th.sortable has no CSS transition on the color property. Adding `transition: color 0.15s ease;` to the th.sortable rule would give a subtle hover fade rather than an instant color switch. Minor UX polish; not required by spec.

app.js sortProjects(): localeCompare() is called without an explicit locale argument (e.g., undefined, { sensitivity: 'base' }). For a local developer tool this is inconsequential, but explicit collation options would make sort order deterministic across different browser locale settings.

styles.css: The '/* Sortable column headers */' section landed at line 511 (after progress-bar rules) rather than directly after the '/* Tables */' block (line 164). Functionally irrelevant, but grouping sort-related header rules alongside the rest of the table styles would improve CSS maintainability.
No observations beyond above — implementation is clean, minimal, mutation-safe (list.slice()), accessibility-aware (aria-sort), and fully consistent with the surrounding vanilla ES5 codebase style.
